The solution is to upgrade the `compile-testing` library to a newer version that doesn't have this issue. Let me check what newer versions are available and if they work with Java 11+.

content.text:
Now I understand the issue completely. In compile-testing version 0.7 (and similar old versions):

1. There is a direct, unconditional dependency on `com.sun:tools` in the main `<dependencies>` section (not in a profile)
2. The profiles only set the `toolsjar` property, but the dependency itself is still required

The fix is to upgrade the `compile-testing` dependency to a newer version that properly handles this. Version 0.19 or later should work. Let me verify by checking version 0.18.

# Build Failure Analysis for google/auto

## Repository: /home/travis/build/failed/google/auto

## Error Description

The build fails with the following error:
```
Could not find artifact com.sun:tools:jar:11.0.27 at specified path /usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64/../lib/tools.jar
```

## Root Cause

The project depends on `compile-testing` library (versions 0.6, 0.7, and 0.8 across different modules). These old versions have an unconditional system-scoped dependency on `com.sun:tools` which points to `tools.jar`.

In Java 8 and earlier, `tools.jar` was located at `$JAVA_HOME/lib/tools.jar` and contained the Java Compiler API and related classes. In Java 9+, this file was removed and its contents were moved into the `jdk.compiler` module.

The project is running on Java 11 where `tools.jar` does not exist, causing the dependency resolution to fail.

## Affected Files

1. **common/pom.xml** - Line 57: uses compile-testing 0.7
2. **service/pom.xml** - Line 58: uses compile-testing 0.6
3. **factory/pom.xml** - Line 74: uses compile-testing 0.8
4. **value/pom.xml** - Line 82: uses compile-testing 0.6

## Solution

Upgrade all `compile-testing` dependencies to version 0.18 or later. Starting from version 0.18, the `com.sun:tools` dependency is moved inside Maven profiles that are only activated when `tools.jar` actually exists. This makes the library compatible with both Java 8 (where tools.jar exists) and Java 9+ (where it doesn't).

Version 0.18 was chosen because:
- It properly handles the tools.jar dependency via conditional profiles
- It's a stable version with good compatibility
- It requires Java 8+ (we're on Java 11, so this is fine)

## Changes Required

| File | Change | Old Value | New Value |
|------|--------|-----------|-----------|
| common/pom.xml | compile-testing version | 0.7 | 0.18 |
| service/pom.xml | compile-testing version | 0.6 | 0.18 |
| factory/pom.xml | compile-testing version | 0.8 | 0.18 |
| value/pom.xml | compile-testing version | 0.6 | 0.18 |

## Patch Files

- patch_1.diff - Updates common/pom.xml
- patch_2.diff - Updates service/pom.xml
- patch_3.diff - Updates factory/pom.xml
- patch_4.diff - Updates value/pom.xml

## Repository: /home/travis/build/failed/google/auto

## Error Description

The build fails with the following error:
```
Could not find artifact com.sun:tools:jar:11.0.27 at specified path /usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64/../lib/tools.jar
```

## Root Cause

The project depends on `compile-testing` library (versions 0.6, 0.7, and 0.8 across different modules). These old versions have an unconditional system-scoped dependency on `com.sun:tools` which points to `tools.jar`.

In Java 8 and earlier, `tools.jar` was located at `$JAVA_HOME/lib/tools.jar` and contained the Java Compiler API and related classes. In Java 9+, this file was removed and its contents were moved into the `jdk.compiler` module.

The project is running on Java 11 where `tools.jar` does not exist, causing the dependency resolution to fail.

## Affected Files

1. **common/pom.xml** - Line 57: uses compile-testing 0.7
2. **service/pom.xml** - Line 58: uses compile-testing 0.6
3. **factory/pom.xml** - Line 74: uses compile-testing 0.8
4. **value/pom.xml** - Line 82: uses compile-testing 0.6

## Solution

Upgrade all `compile-testing` dependencies to version 0.18 or later. Starting from version 0.18, the `com.sun:tools` dependency is moved inside Maven profiles that are only activated when `tools.jar` actually exists. This makes the library compatible with both Java 8 (where tools.jar exists) and Java 9+ (where it doesn't).

Version 0.18 was chosen because:
- It properly handles the tools.jar dependency via conditional profiles
- It's a stable version with good compatibility
- It requires Java 8+ (we're on Java 11, so this is fine)

|------|--------|-----------|-----------|
| common/pom.xml | compile-testing version | 0.7 | 0.18 |
| service/pom.xml | compile-testing version | 0.6 | 0.18 |
| factory/pom.xml | compile-testing version | 0.8 | 0.18 |
| value/pom.xml | compile-testing version | 0.6 | 0.18 |

- patch_2.diff - Updates service/pom.xml
- patch_3.diff - Updates factory/pom.xml
- patch_4.diff - Updates value/pom.xml

  </parent>

  <groupId>com.google.auto.value</groupId>

  <version>1.2-SNAPSHOT</version>
  <name>AutoValue</name>
  <description>
    Immutable value-type code generation for Java 1.6+.
  </description>

  <properties>
    <guava.version>18.0</guava.version>
  </properties>
  <scm>
    <url>http://github.com/google/auto</url>
    <connection>scm:git:git://github.com/google/auto.git</connection>
    <developerConnection>scm:git:ssh://git@github.com/google/auto.git</developerConnection>
    <tag>HEAD</tag>
  </scm>

  <dependencies>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.auto</groupId>
      <artifactId>auto-common</artifactId>
      <version>1.0-SNAPSHOT</version>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.auto.service</groupId>
      <artifactId>auto-service</artifactId>
      <version>1.0-rc2</version>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.guava</groupId>
      <artifactId>guava</artifactId>
      <version>${guava.version}</version>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.ow2.asm</groupId>
      <artifactId>asm</artifactId>
      <version>4.1</version>
    </dependency>
    <!-- test dependencies -->
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.apache.velocity</groupId>
      <artifactId>velocity</artifactId>
      <version>1.7</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.guava</groupId>
      <artifactId>guava-testlib</artifactId>
      <version>${guava.version}</version>
      <scope>test</scope>

    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.testing.compile</groupId>
      <artifactId>compile-testing</artifactId>
      <version>0.18</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>junit</groupId>
      <artifactId>junit</artifactId>
      <version>4.11</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.truth</groupId>
      <artifactId>truth</artifactId>
      <version>0.25</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
  </dependencies>

  <build>
    <resources>
      <resource>
        <directory>src/main/java</directory>
      </resource>
    </resources>
    <plugins>
      <plugin>
        <artifactId>maven-jar-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>2.5</version>
      </plugin>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
        <artifactId>maven-invoker-plugin</artifactId>
        <configuration>
          <addTestClassPath>true</addTestClassPath>
          <cloneProjectsTo>${project.build.directory}/it</cloneProjectsTo>
          <filterProperties>
            <auto.version>${project.version}</auto.version>
          </filterProperties>
          <pomIncludes>
            <pomInclude>*/pom.xml</pomInclude>
          </pomIncludes>
          <streamLogs>true</streamLogs>
        </configuration>
        <executions>
          <execution>
            <id>integration-test</id>
            <goals>
              <goal>install</goal>
              <goal>run</goal>
            </goals>
          </execution>
        </executions>
      </plugin>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.immutables.tools</groupId>
        <artifactId>maven-shade-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>3</version>
        <executions>
          <execution>
            <phase>package</phase>
            <goals>
              <goal>shade</goal>
            </goals>
            <configuration>
              <minimizeJar>true</minimizeJar>
              <relocations>
                <relocation>
                  <pattern>org.objectweb</pattern>
                  <shadedPattern>autovalue.shaded.org.objectweb$</shadedPattern>
                </relocation>
                <relocation>
                  <pattern>com.google</pattern>
                  <shadedPattern>autovalue.shaded.com.google$</shadedPattern>
                  <excludes>
                    <exclude>com.google.auto.value.**</exclude>
                  </excludes>
                </relocation>
              </relocations>
            </configuration>
          </execution>
        </executions>
      </plugin>
    </plugins>
  </build>
</project>
